description:
In today's Daily Fix:
Rockstar finally dropped their extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6, and the game looks as dense as any GTA game before it. In fact, according to Rockstar, the map for GTA 6 is twice the size of GTA 5's, and three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar North's co-studio head Rob Nelson also revealed that it took him about 80 hours to finish the game while primarily focusing on story missions. In other news, eagle-eyed fans spotted a Red Dead 2 easter egg in the new GTA 6 footage. Plus we’re riding Mine Cart Madness inside Super Nintendo World with The Ride Guys at Universal Epic Universe at Universal Orlando Resort.

Presented by Universal Orlando Resort, and its newest theme park, Universal Epic Universe.

author: IGN
description:
Grand Theft Auto III legacy review by Luke Reilly. Reviewed on PlayStation 2. 

"Grand Theft Auto III, in its original form, is a frustrating and regularly cumbersome game to play in 2026. Its unforgiving need to manually return to mission markers and start from scratch encourages a very careful and conservative sort of playstyle that clashes with the chaotic level of freedom its world and systems otherwise encourage. On top of this, its shooting is admittedly fussy and frustrating, and its cast of shallow and simplistic characters are amongst the least memorable of the series. Within that initial salvo of 3D GTA games, Vice City oozed dramatically more style and swagger, and San Andreas offered astonishingly increased size and scope. However, neither of these legendary games can lay claim to being GTA III – just improved versions of it.
It occupies a unique place in the series' storied history. While it didn’t pioneer every part of the modern formula for open-world games, it brought
title: Grand Theft Auto III – The Legacy Review

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the most anticipated game of at least the last decade. And we got the chance to go Rockstar North and watch co-studio head Rob Nelson play through 30 minutes of the game. 

Half an hour later, it has become a clear and uncontestable fact that this game will occupy every waking minute of my existence when it finally arrives this November. When IGN was invited into the secretive halls of Rockstar North for an exclusive look, we knew the gameplay slice would show how much GTA has grown and evolved since its last iteration launched 13 years ago.
